bibliography.abstract: Abstract Accurate geolocation of Early Years Providers in England is important for understanding the spatial distribution of childcare provision and for supporting service planning, equity monitoring, and linkage to other administrative and spatial datasets. However, provider records in the Ofsted Childcare Providers and Inspections dataset do not routinely include Unique Property Reference Numbers, requiring retrospective address matching. We evaluated five address-matching approaches for assigning Unique Property Reference Numbers to 6,442 Early Years Provider records from the 2017 Ofsted register extract. Preprocessing was standardised across methods. A stratified validation subset enriched for agreement, disagreement, and candidate ambiguity was manually reviewed to assign AddressBase® Premium reference identifiers for 585 records, of which 565 had a definitive AddressBase® Premium identifier. Linkage was defined as whether a method returned at least one Unique Property Reference Number. For methods returning a single identifier, matching performance was assessed using precision, recall, and the F1 score against the AddressBase® Premium reference. For the Ordnance Survey Match & Cleanse API, evaluation used a candidate-set match definition rather than deterministic selection of a single final identifier. Because the approaches differed in output structure and decision rules, results should be interpreted as a comparison of practical UPRN linkage workflows rather than a like-for-like comparison of algorithms. Within the validation subset, linkage coverage ranged from 51% to 99%. Among single-output methods, ASSIGN 1 and the bespoke SQL workflow provided the most balanced precision–recall profile. High linkage coverage did not guarantee correct matching. Routine inclusion of Unique Property Reference Numbers within childcare provider registers would strengthen the spatial visibility of early years provision and support more reliable planning and cross-sector linkage.
bibliography.title: Improving the Property-Level Identification of Early Years Providers in England: A Comparison of Practical UPRN Linkage Approaches

en.caveats: Because the tested approaches relied on varied input parameters, preprocessing techniques, and decision rules, the study compares practical workflows rather than isolated algorithmic performance.
en.what: Five address-matching workflows were evaluated to assign Unique Property Reference Numbers (UPRNs) to 6,442 non-domestic early years childcare providers in England using the 2018 Ofsted extract. Performance was validated against 558 manually reviewed records, showing that linkage coverage spanned from 51% to 100%, while top-performing approaches achieved unweighted F1 scores of 0.707 and 0.712.
en.why: This evaluation establishes that high address-linkage rates do not reliably indicate accuracy, providing practical baseline performance metrics for researchers attaching property identifiers to administrative childcare registers.
